question: Can an employee carry forward unused annual leave to the next year?
reference_answer: Yes. An employee may postpone annual leave or some of it to the following year with employer approval. An employer may also postpone annual leave for up to 90 days after the entitlement year when work circumstances require it. Further postponement requires written employee consent and is subject to statutory limits.
reference_contexts:
Law ID: LAW044
Category: Annual Leave
Article: 110
Title: Employee Postponement
Rule: An employee may postpone annual leave or some days of it to the following year with employer approval.
Conditions: Employer approval is required.
Exceptions: Further postponement is subject to statutory limits.

Law ID: LAW045
Category: Annual Leave
Article: 110
Title: Employer Postponement
Rule: An employer may postpone annual leave after the entitlement year for up to 90 days when work circumstances require it.
Conditions: Business circumstances must justify postponement.
Exceptions: Further postponement requires written employee consent and cannot extend beyond the end of the following year.

question: What is the minimum annual leave under Saudi labor law?
reference_answer: An employee is entitled to at least 21 days of annual leave for each year of service, subject to applicable eligibility and service rules.
reference_contexts:
Law ID: LAW037
Category: Annual Leave
Article: 109
Title: Minimum Annual Leave
Rule: An employee is entitled to annual leave of at least 21 days for each year of service.
Conditions: Applies to eligible employees.
Exceptions: Service and employment status rules apply.

question: How many days of annual leave does an employee get after five years of service?
reference_answer: Annual leave increases to at least 30 days when the employee completes five consecutive years of service with the employer, subject to applicable service rules.
reference_contexts:
Law ID: LAW038
Category: Annual Leave
Article: 109
Title: Annual Leave After Five Years
Rule: Annual leave increases to at least 30 days when the employee completesfive consecutive years of service with the employer.
Conditions: Five consecutive years of service are required.
Exceptions: Applicable service rules apply.

question: How is overtime compensated?
reference_answer: Overtime is compensated at the hourly wage plus 50 percent of the basic wage, provided the hours qualify as overtime under the Labor Law. Alternative paid compensatory leave may be used with employee consent under applicable rules.
reference_contexts:
Law ID: LAW033
Category: Overtime
Article: 107
Title: Overtime Compensation
Rule: Overtime is compensated at the hourly wage plus 50 percent of the basic wage.
Conditions: The hours must qualify as overtime under the Labor Law.
Exceptions: Alternative paid compensatory leave may be used with employee consent under applicable rules.

question: What must an employee do when they get sick and miss work?
reference_answer: The employee must notify their Department Head on the first day of sickness and provide the required medical certificate. The medical documentation must be provided through an accredited authority.

question: Can the employer deduct money from my salary for damage I caused?
reference_answer: An employer may deduct amounts from an employee's wage for damage caused by the employee, subject to the conditions and limits established by the Labor Law.

question: What is the purpose of the Wage Protection System?
reference_answer: The Wage Protection Program monitors wage payments and improves wage transparency for establishments subject to the program.

question: How can an establishment access the Wage Protection System?
reference_answer: An establishment can access the Wage Protection System through the Mudad platform.

question: When does the Wage Protection System generate an alert because the current wage is less than half of the registered wage?
reference_answer: The Wage Protection System generates an alert when the current wage is less than 50 percent of the registered wage.

question: When does the Wage Protection System generate an alert because deductions are too high?
reference_answer: The Wage Protection System generates an alert when deductions exceed 50 percent of total entitlements.

question: When does the Wage Protection System flag a gap between wage payments for a monthly-paid employee?
reference_answer: The Wage Protection System flags a gap when the period between wage payments for a monthly-paid employee exceeds 30 days.

question: What can happen if an uploaded Wage Protection file contains invalid data or an invalid IBAN?
reference_answer: Invalid data or an invalid IBAN in an uploaded Wage Protection file can cause the file to fail processing or be rejected.

question: Can an employer submit a justification for a Wage Protection violation?
reference_answer: Yes. An employer can submit a justification for a Wage Protection violation through the applicable process.

question: Can an employee accept or reject an employer's justification for a Wage Protection violation?
reference_answer: Yes. An employee can accept or reject an employer's submitted justification for a Wage Protection violation.

question: What information is included in the employee payment details in the Wage Protection file?
reference_answer: Employee payment details in the Wage Protection file can include the employee's bank account or card information, employee name, bank identifier, and payment details.

question: What are the different types of wage components that can be included in a Wage Protection file?
reference_answer: Wage components can include basic wage, housing allowance, other payments, and total entitlements.

question: How can an establishment verify its Wage Protection compliance certificate?
reference_answer: The Mudad platform provides access to wage protection certificate services for eligible establishments. The policy texts do not describe a specific verification procedure.

question: Does the company have a policy about employees working remotely from Mars?
reference_answer: There is no relevant company policy covering employees working remotely from Mars. The system should state that the available policy sources do not contain this information rather than inventing a policy.
